Thomson made an ingenious modification to his experiment to measure the velocity of the electrons directly and thereby determine e/me. He established a mag- netic field in the same region as the electric field by passing an electric current through a pair of coils, as shown in Figure 1.9. The magnetic field was oriented perpendicular to both the electric field and to the flight path of the electrons, and it exerted an upward force on them. Thomson could return the deflected beam to its original position by varying the strengths of the two fields so that the net force on the electrons was zero. The force due to the electric field E was
